# Samuṭṭhānavāra (Pvr 1.5)

**ID:** Pvr 1.5
**Section:** Parivāra (pvr)
**Collection:** Vinaya
**Title (Pali):** Samuṭṭhānavāra
**tipitaka.org (CST):** https://tipitaka.org/romn/cscd/vin02m4.mul0.xml

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Samuṭṭhānavāra* ("The number of originations of each offense") constitutes the fifth section of the first division of the *Parivāra* in the Pali Vinaya Piṭaka. The text analyzes and classifies monastic transgressions according to the channels of their origination (*samuṭṭhāna*), defining offenses based on whether they originate through body, speech, mind, or permutations of the three. As Oskar von Hinüber notes, *samuṭṭhāna* is a distinctive Vinaya technical concept, and the division of the *Parivāra* into *vāras* represents its broader role as a systematic handbook of the Vinaya compiled for practical application [von Hinüber 1996]. I.B. Horner similarly observes that the analysis of the origins of offenses is a fundamental topic recurrently excerpted and organized across several chapters of the *Parivāra* [Horner 1966]. An English translation of the section has been published by Bhikkhu Brahmali.

 Within the Pali Canon, DharmaNexus registers dense internal text reuse amounting to 157 matching passages across 21 texts, reflecting the standardized analytical formulae of the Vinaya [DharmaNexus]. The vast majority of these correspondences occur within the *Parivāra* itself, showing substantial overlap with the *Katthapaññattivāra* (Pvr 1.1; 73 matches), other *Samuṭṭhānavāra* sections (such as Pvr 2.13, Pvr 2.5, and Pvr 1.13), and the *Atthāpattisamuṭṭhāna* (Pvr 18) [DharmaNexus]. Secondary literature appearing in the dossier otherwise mentions *samuṭṭhāna* solely in connection with Abhidhammic psychological causation, bodily humors in medicine, or Suttanta classifications of views.
